analysis.requirement: R4 — Out-of-sample spatial validation of the shelter-placement result (demand from an earlier period, sites selected blind to holdout, evaluation on a later period; spatially blocked CV; campsite-location uncertainty; baselines = current facilities, random sites, capacity-only, conventional p-median, equity-oriented; consistency across holdouts; ideally second-city transfer)
exists_defensible: The in-sample circularity is disclosed as the FIRST limitation in both manuscript forms, with the correct 'upper bound' conclusion: 'The optimizer is evaluated on the demand it was fitted to... C's advantage over B is therefore an upper bound on what the same procedure would achieve against a distribution of campsites it had not seen' (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:297; same text quoted from Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:861 in docs/critique-response/02-parameters.md:350-357).

The manuscript's own future-work list names the exact R4 fix as its fourth extension: 'the placement procedure should be fitted on one set of campsite locations and evaluated on another' (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:321) — the project knows what is missing.

An internal adversarial review fully diagnoses the problem and prescribes the remedy: 'fitted and evaluated on one and the same point set. There is no hold-out, no resampling of campsite locations, no spatial cross-validation... The scientific fix... is to re-run the optimiser against a held-out or perturbed campsite draw and report the degraded gap' (docs/critique-response/02-parameters.md:332-346, 369-391).

Three of the five required baselines exist, albeit in-sample only: (1) current facilities = scenario A and (2) capacity-only placement = scenario B's uniform 3.06x scale-up at existing coordinates (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:182-184), both archived across 9 seeds (docs/runs/present-day-three-arm/); (3) random sites = the CR/CP random-pool control, 18 archived runs verified present (docs/runs/scenario-crandom-2026/CR2026r1-3 and CP2026r4-6 x seeds 42-44, simulation.json in each).

The random-sites control was used with real discipline: it demoted the optimizer's headcount claim ('Ten sites drawn uniformly at random from the same 498-node candidate pool... reproduce C's sheltered count exactly, in every seed', md:238), and the deck states 'This control refuted my own headline' (docs/final/presentation/capacity-is-not-access-symposium.html:340).

A min-cost-flow bound shows C's admissions are at the coordination optimum for its site set (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:238) — an internal optimality check on the headcount channel.

The 63.1% walking edge has a clean provenance chain and is correctly scoped in the deck as walking-only and awareness-conditional (docs/PRESENTATION_PROVENANCE.md:56-59: C 3-seed mean walk 5,537 m vs random-pool 15,011 m; deck html:334-337); it is not claimed in the manuscript at all.

The machinery to run holdout experiments is committed and re-runnable: scripts/build_scenario_c_2026.py (greedy capacitated p-median, GRID_M=600, MAX_CANDIDATES=500, demand read at line 33), scripts/build_scenario_crandom_2026.py and build_scenario_crandom_pool_2026.py (random-site baselines), and the fitted demand surface is archived in-repo (docs/runs/present-day-three-arm/B-seed42/agents.csv verified present).

The 9-seed design (seeds 42-50, 27 runs) with everything except the shelter file held identical (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:190) gives a clean paired-comparison scaffold that any holdout protocol can reuse.
missing: ABSENT: any spatial hold-out or spatially blocked cross-validation of site selection — stated flatly by the repo's own review: 'no hold-out, no resampling of campsite locations, no spatial cross-validation' (docs/critique-response/02-parameters.md:344-346).

ABSENT: any temporal split (demand from an earlier period, evaluation on a later period). All 27 runs use one fixed demand file; the optimizer reads a single agents.csv (scripts/build_scenario_c_2026.py:33). The campsite CSV carries a per-row inc_date column (header verified) but no analysis anywhere uses it for splitting.

ABSENT: campsite-location uncertainty quantification. The 3,400 rows are individual complaint reports with unique incident ids, not deduplicated sites (data-inventory verified); no bootstrap, positional jitter, deduplication sensitivity, or report-vs-site analysis exists; visibility bias is acknowledged only qualitatively (md:93, md:307 per inventory).

ABSENT: an equity-oriented placement baseline. D3 'equity-objective placement' is on the deferred/descoped list (docs/critique-response/11-ROUND5-REPORT.md:254-260, per validation inventory); no such run family exists in docs/runs/.

ABSENT: a 'novel method vs conventional p-median' comparison — structurally unavailable, because the method IS a conventional greedy capacitated p-median heuristic (md:188; build_scenario_c_2026.py:17-20). There is no exact-solver benchmark either, so even the heuristic's optimality gap on the walking objective is unquantified (the min-cost-flow bound covers admissions only, md:238). This substantially weakens the IJGIS 'genuinely new methodological contribution' pathway.
ABSENT: any consistency-across-holdouts reporting — impossible by construction since no holdouts exist.

ABSENT: second-city or second-event transfer of any kind — one county, one event, one street network; Scenario-E severities are counterfactual transforms of the same event (validation inventory, verified against docs/runs/ enumeration).
ABSENT: any out-of-sample estimate of the 63.1% (or 25.2% B-to-C) walking-distance edge — the only number the optimizer still owns after the headcount demotion.

ABSENT: propagation of the in-sample caveat outside the chapter — verified missing from docs/final/PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md (its only 'upper bound' instance, lines 284-286, is the awareness caveat) and from docs/runs/scenario-c-2026-new-sites/scenario_c_report.json:91-96 (four limitations listed, circularity not among them); also reported missing from README.md (02-parameters.md:362-365).
implementable_with_existing_data: Temporal holdout within the available window: split Geography/data/encampments/irp_campsite_reports_sample.csv on its inc_date column (header verified: lon, lat, inc_date, inc_id, is_vehicle; spans 2025-01..2026-07 per Geography/data/README.md:171-172), fit the p-median on the earlier half's demand, evaluate the chosen site set on the later half via scripts/build_scenario_c_2026.py's assignment routine or full model runs. Honest caveat: this validates within the 2025-26 proxy vintage — it cannot reach 2020, because zero 2020 rows exist in the feed.

Spatially blocked k-fold CV: assign campsite reports to spatial blocks (grid cells or contiguous quadrants, sized larger than the 600 m candidate-thinning cell at build_scenario_c_2026.py:40), fit sites on k-1 blocks, score walking distance and refusals on the held-out block, and report the fold-wise degradation of the C-vs-B gap. Everything needed is in-repo: the street graph (Geography/data/Streets.*, built via scripts/test_routing.py build_graphs), the shelter inventory (Geography/data/shelters/shelters_2026_current_placement.csv), and the archived demand surface (docs/runs/present-day-three-arm/B-seed42/agents.csv).

Campsite-location uncertainty: nonparametric bootstrap over the 3,400 report rows, positional jitter at plausible report precision, and a deduplication-radius sensitivity (cluster reports within X m into sites, sweep X) — propagate each draw through the optimizer and report the site-set stability (e.g., Jaccard overlap) and a CI on the walking edge. The is_vehicle column additionally supports an exclude-vehicle-reports sensitivity.

Equity-oriented placement baseline: modify the greedy objective in scripts/build_scenario_c_2026.py to p-center/max-min or mobility-weighted distance — the per-agent mobility attributes already exist in the archived agents.csv files; no new data required.

Exact-solver p-median benchmark: solve the integer program on the same <=500-candidate pool (MAX_CANDIDATES=500, build_scenario_c_2026.py:41) to quantify the greedy heuristic's optimality gap on the walking objective — closes the 'conventional p-median' baseline requirement in the only form available to this project.

Baseline consistency table: rerun the existing CR/CP random-site protocol (scripts/build_scenario_crandom_pool_2026.py; archives at docs/runs/scenario-crandom-2026/) and the A/B arms under each spatial/temporal fold, and report whether optimized placement beats random on walking distance in every fold — the R4 'consistent improvement across holdouts' statement.
needs_new_empirical_data: Independent encampment enumeration to quantify complaint-report visibility bias: a systematic street-segment field count (PIT-style protocol, locations recorded at aggregated precision) compared against the complaint-report surface for the same period.

Prospective shelter arrival/occupancy logging during a future smoke event (instrument: a simple per-facility hourly census protocol agreed with county shelter operators) — the only way to obtain a true later-period behavioral evaluation target.

A stated- or revealed-preference survey of shelter destination choice among unsheltered residents (instrument: short intercept survey on distance tolerance and known-facility sets) to validate that network walking distance is the right placement objective at all.
needs_external_acquisition: Pre-2025 extracts of the Portland campsite-report feed to lengthen the temporal-split window (candidate source: City of Portland HUCIRP / open-data program via records request; candidate source: Internet Archive snapshots of the ArcGIS feed). The repo records that the public feed retains only a rolling recent window with zero 2020 records (Geography/data/README.md:171-172) — availability of archived extracts is unverified.

Multnomah County / JOHS after-action documentation and any per-facility occupancy records for Sept 2020 (candidate source: county public-records request) — the repo notes these were never obtained (SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT per validation inventory); would supply the later-period evaluation side for the historical arm.

Second-city replication data for transferability (candidate sources: Seattle/King County encampment-report feed plus shelter inventory; LAHSA for the January 2025 Los Angeles fires; Oregon HMIS for Salem/Eugene during the same 2020 event). Availability and comparability unverified — these are candidate sources only. ERL effectively requires this; IJGIS may not.
Sub-county PIT count geography from the local CoC (candidate source: OR-501 Continuum of Care) as an independent demand surface to cross-check the complaint-report proxy.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'The optimiser contributes zero to headcount and 63.1% shorter walks'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The 63.1% walking edge is computed on the identical demand surface the optimizer was fitted to (02-parameters.md:334-346). The deck conditions the number on universal awareness but not on in-sample fitting; no out-of-sample estimate exists anywhere, so the deck presents an upper bound as the optimizer's contribution without saying so.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: C 96.0% vs B 91.6% (and the walking reductions) presented without the in-sample caveat
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/final/PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md (verified: the file's only 'upper bound' statement, lines 284-286, is the awareness caveat A-12, not the fitted-demand caveat)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The chapter's first limitation (md:297) is not propagated: a reader of the results doc receives the C-vs-B margin as unconditional. The repo's own review calls this 'inconsistent propagation' (02-parameters.md:384-388).

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: scenario_c_report.json 'limitations' array omits the circularity entirely
claims_exceeding_evidence.location: docs/runs/scenario-c-2026-new-sites/scenario_c_report.json:91-96 (verified: four limitations listed — node-sites, heuristic, policy parameters, no construction cost — none is fitted-demand evaluation)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The machine-readable record of scenario C, the artifact most likely to travel with the data, carries every limitation except the one R4 is about.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'the same 6,842 spaces more than halve refusals depending only on placement'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: States the in-sample 550-to-244 refusal halving as a general property of placement with no in-sentence upper-bound conditioning; under R4 the honest phrasing is 'halved refusals against the demand surface the placement was fitted to.'

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'The present 36-facility system shelters 30.1% of residents... Spending the identical capacity on ten better-placed sites shelters 96.0%'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Present-tense declaratives about the real system from unvalidated in-sample model output; hedged elsewhere (md:289, md:297) but not in the sentences a reviewer will quote.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'The result is a good placement, not a provably optimal one'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: 'Good' is asserted without out-of-sample support and without an optimality-gap benchmark on the walking objective — the min-cost-flow bound (md:238) certifies admissions only, and admissions were shown to be placement-indifferent by the random-pool control.

proposed_methods: Spatially blocked k-fold cross-validation (block CV in the Roberts et al. 2017 sense): grid or contiguous-region blocks strictly larger than the 600 m candidate-thinning cell; fit the capacitated p-median on training blocks, evaluate walking distance and refusals on held-out blocks; report the fold-wise distribution of the C-vs-B gap and the worst fold, not just the mean.

Temporal fit/holdout split on inc_date within 2025-01..2026-07 (fit on 2025 reports, evaluate on 2026, and reversed), reporting how much of the in-sample walking edge survives; state explicitly that this tests transfer across the proxy window, not to 2020.

Campsite-location uncertainty propagation: nonparametric bootstrap of report rows + positional jitter + deduplication-radius sweep, propagated through the optimizer; report site-set stability (Jaccard overlap of chosen sites across draws) and a confidence interval on the walking edge.

Full baseline suite evaluated under every holdout: current facilities (A), capacity-only scale-up (B), random sites from the candidate pool (existing CR/CP protocol), exact-solver p-median (integer program on the <=500-candidate pool, quantifying the greedy heuristic's optimality gap), and an equity-oriented placement (p-center/max-min or mobility-weighted objective) — with paired per-fold, per-seed comparisons.

A pre-registered consistency criterion in the project's own prediction-registration style (cf. docs/critique-response/12/13-*PREDICTIONS.md): e.g., 'optimized placement beats random-pool placement on mean walking distance in every spatial fold and both temporal directions' — scored hit/miss like Phase D/E.

Transferability: replicate the fitted-vs-holdout pipeline in one additional city/event if external data is acquired; failing that, reframe the IJGIS contribution as a validation-protocol and attribution-discipline contribution (the random-pool demotion is genuinely publishable) rather than a siting-method contribution, and scope all placement numbers to Portland as upper bounds.

Editorial propagation fix (cheap, immediate): copy the md:297/tex:861 limitation sentence into PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md, README.md, scenario_c_report.json's limitations array, and the deck's optimizer slide, and add a claims.yaml linter rule requiring 'upper bound' within range of any 96.0-vs-91.6 or 63.1% statement — mirroring the existing 1.52x/15.6 bracket rule (docs/claims.yaml:129-151).
analysis.priority_rationale: R4 is the most load-bearing external-validity requirement for this project's placement finding, because of what the project's own controls have already established. The random-pool control demoted the optimizer's headcount contribution to zero (md:238; 18 archived runs verified at docs/runs/scenario-crandom-2026/), so the ONLY quantified advantage the siting procedure still owns is the walking-distance edge — 63.1% vs random-pool in the deck, 25.2% B-to-C in the results — and that edge is entirely in-sample: fitted and evaluated on one point set, with 'no hold-out, no resampling, no spatial cross-validation' by the repo's own verdict (02-parameters.md:344-346, 369-380). If the walking edge does not survive holdout evaluation, scenario C reduces to 'dispersion helps', which the random control already proves without any optimizer. The methodological-novelty escape hatch for a Portland-only IJGIS paper is weak here, since the method is a conventional greedy capacitated p-median (md:188; build_scenario_c_2026.py:17-20) — so acceptance would rest almost entirely on validation rigor, which is exactly the absent piece. The mitigating facts are real: the circularity is disclosed as the chapter's first limitation with the correct upper-bound conclusion (md:297), the fix is already named as future work in the manuscript itself (md:321), three of the five required baselines exist in-sample, and the dated campsite reports (inc_date column verified) plus committed optimizer scripts make spatial-block CV, a within-window temporal split, and location-uncertainty bootstraps implementable now with zero new data collection. What existing data cannot deliver is validation against the 2020 event (no 2020 campsite rows exist) or any second city — the former needs external acquisition of archived report extracts or county records, the latter is mandatory for ERL and strongly advisable for IJGIS. Until holdout results exist, every placement advantage must be quoted as an upper bound everywhere it appears, and currently it is not (PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md, scenario_c_report.json:91-96, and the deck all omit the caveat).
